frame.restated: An adversary with existing access to Windows hosts on this network harvested credentials from those hosts.
frame.what_would_confirm: LSASS memory access or dumping (e.g., procdump, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, Mimikatz), SAM/SECURITY hive or NTDS.dit extraction, credential-store or DPAPI access, Kerberoasting/AS-REP roasting, or suspicious access to lsass.exe by non-standard processes.
frame.what_would_refute: No evidence of credential-dumping tooling or LSASS/hive access, no anomalous authentication with harvested credentials, and no credential-theft artifacts across the affected hosts.

verdict.rule: Confirmed if >=1 in-scope incident of verified malicious findings (confidence >= medium); Inconclusive if only suspicious incidents or coverage gaps; Refuted if full coverage and no malicious/suspicious finding

T1003.name: OS Credential Dumping
T1003.reason: Credential-theft staging and anti-forensic cleanup on scranton/nashua (C:\ProgramData\victim\…cod.3aka3.scr, sdelete64 wiping of the payload and archives) surrounding the LSASS memory access.

T1003.001.name: LSASS Memory
T1003.001.reason: PowerShell.exe (pbeesly, high integrity) opened lsass.exe with 0x1F3FFF/0x1FFFFF and read process memory (0x10) on scranton at 03:05:16; wsmprovhost.exe did the same with 0x1F3FFF on nashua at 03:09:29.

T1003.002.name: Security Account Manager
T1003.002.reason: Ten 4656 SAM_SERVER handle requests with AccessMask 0xf003f on scranton between 03:19:21Z and 03:20:46Z, concurrent with the anchored LSASS access and sdelete anti-forensics; requester is lsass.exe as SYSTEM, so no hive copy was observed.

T1003.003.name: NTDS
T1003.003.reason: No ntdsutil/vssadmin/diskshadow/ntds.dit activity in process creation, file creation or PowerShell script blocks.

T1003.004.name: LSA Secrets
T1003.004.reason: No access to SECURITY\Policy\Secrets registry keys, no lsadump/secrets command lines and no SECURITY object access events.

T1003.005.name: Cached Domain Credentials
T1003.005.reason: No cached-credential (SECURITY hive / Cache) object access or lsadump cache commands were observed.

T1003.006.name: DCSync
T1003.006.reason: Only one 4662 DS Control Access event by machine account NEWYORK$ with mask 0x100; no DS-Replication-Get-Changes access, no drsuapi/DCSync tooling.

T1040.name: Network Sniffing
T1040.reason: Only packet-capture activity observed is netsh.exe 'trace start capture=yes' / 'trace stop' on scranton.dmevals.local, spawned as SYSTEM by the signed Azure Network Watcher Agent (NetworkWatcherAgent.exe) alongside Azure guest-agent logman ETW session cycling. No pktmon/npcap/winpcap driver loads, no tcpdump/windump/rawcap/dumpcap usage in sysmon or PowerShell, and no sniffing-related Zeek notices. Capture is sanctioned platform monitoring, not adversary network sniffing.

T1056.name: Input Capture
T1056.reason: PowerShell.exe (PID 2976, SYSTEM) on scranton opened lsass.exe with 0x1F3FFF and 0x1FFFFF and UNKNOWN call-trace frames at 03:05:16Z, inside a broader hidden-PowerShell intrusion chain by pbeesly.

T1056.001.name: Keylogging
T1056.001.reason: Invoke-ScreenCapture script block on scranton loops CopyFromScreen every 300s and saves BMPs to the user's Downloads; a .bmp file creation by powershell.exe corroborates execution. Screen-based capture, no keylogger APIs found.

T1056.002.name: GUI Input Capture
T1056.002.reason: Three consent.exe UAC prompt creations exist and scranton shows a 'Start-Process hostui.exe -verb runas' elevation, but individual consent events were not retrieved, so a fake credential prompt is unconfirmed.

T1056.003.name: Web Portal Capture
T1056.003.reason: No inetpub/aspx file writes, no 4663 inetpub access, no HTTP POST; the only related hits were archive staging of *login*/*pass* files, which is collection not web-portal capture.

T1056.004.name: Credential API Hooking
T1056.004.reason: lsass handles with near-full access from PowerShell on scranton (UNKNOWN call trace) and from wsmprovhost.exe on nashua (0x1F3FFF, UNKNOWN frames) indicate credential-API abuse; no MiniDump script block was logged.

T1110.name: Brute Force
T1110.reason: Zero 4625 failed logons in windows.security; the 15 4648 events are pbeesly's own explicit-credential logons plus normal winlogon/wininit/taskhostw machine-account logons. No brute-force tooling in process command lines.

T1110.001.name: Password Guessing
T1110.001.reason: No failed authentication attempts at all (4625 count 0); PowerShell 'Password' hits are certificate export and 7-Zip archive passwords, not guessing loops.

T1110.002.name: Password Cracking
T1110.002.reason: No offline cracking tooling or NTDS/SAM hive dumps were seen, but on scranton.dmevals.local hidden PowerShell PID 2976 (spawned by control.exe, shellcode stager) opened lsass.exe with 0x1f3fff and 0x1fffff — the credential-theft precursor whose output would be cracked offline.

T1110.003.name: Password Spraying
T1110.003.reason: No 4625 failures and no multi-account authentication from a single source; pbeesly's 4648s are one account reused via PSEXESVC.exe on nashua.dmevals.local (lateral movement), not a spray.

T1110.004.name: Credential Stuffing
T1110.004.reason: No failed logons and no username/password list replay scripts; password strings found in script blocks belong to cert export and archive compression.

T1111.name: Multi-Factor Authentication Interception
T1111.reason: No smartcard/MFA tooling or interception artifacts; lsass access and 4648 logons are credential theft/reuse and exfiltration.

T1187.name: Forced Authentication
T1187.reason: On scranton.dmevals.local, PowerShell (user pbeesly) hijacked HKCU\Software\Classes\Folder\shell\open\command with a hidden -ep bypass PowerShell payload and dropped hostui.lnk into the all-users StartUp folder via Invoke-Persistence, the classic forced-authentication/shell-handler abuse pattern; the session also harvested private keys and clipboard data. NTLM network logon and LsaSrv 6038 NTLM-use events on the same host corroborate NTLM authentication being exercised.

T1212.name: Exploitation for Credential Access
T1212.reason: On scranton.dmevals.local a hidden, execution-policy-bypassing PowerShell (PID 2976, child of control.exe, running as DMEVALS\pbeesly at High integrity) opened lsass.exe with GrantedAccess 0x1F3FFF and 0x1FFFFF at 03:05:16Z with an UNKNOWN-module call trace — full-access LSASS handles consistent with in-memory credential dumping, followed by exfiltration and lateral PowerShell to NASHUA. A related wsmprovhost.exe lsass access (0x1F3FFF) on nashua.dmevals.local is suspicious; the wininit/csrss/svchost lsass handles are benign system behaviour.

T1539.name: Steal Web Session Cookie
T1539.reason: No event shows a browser cookie/session store being read or copied by a non-browser process. Cookie-related hits resolve to Windows Search indexing (SearchProtocolHost.exe under SearchIndexer.exe), substring matches on lastalive*.dat / GroupPolicy paths, and a normal MicrosoftEdge.exe launch by pbeesly on scranton creating its own profile files. No 4663 object access on cookie paths and no sysmon handle (event.code 10) to a browser image. The attacker toolkit on scranton (pbeesly) does harvest certificates, screenshots and exfiltrate, but not web session cookies.

T1552.name: Unsecured Credentials
T1552.reason: accesschk.exe created C:\Program Files\SysinternalsSuite\passwordsDB inside the malicious pbeesly session; content unverified, other hits are OS noise.

T1552.001.name: Credentials In Files
T1552.001.reason: PowerShell on nashua enumerated the user profile for *pass*/*psw*/*login*/*vpn*/*.pst/*.txt/*.lnk files and compressed them to working.zip, then Rar.exe password-protected the archive and sdelete64 wiped it; on scranton the same operator used the plaintext password Fl0nk3rt0n!T0by with PsExec64.

T1552.002.name: Credentials in Registry
T1552.002.reason: Only OS-generated registry writes to Credential/Password paths; no reg query/save or SAM/SECURITY access.

T1552.003.name: Shell History
T1552.003.reason: No ConsoleHost_history, Get-History or PSReadline references in sysmon or PowerShell logs.

T1552.004.name: Private Keys
T1552.004.reason: Get-PrivateKeys exported LocalMachine certificates to .pfx with hardcoded password saribas; coyn5igj.3io.pfx created on scranton.

T1552.006.name: Group Policy Preferences
T1552.006.reason: No Groups.xml/cpassword/SYSVOL/gpp references; only normal gpt.ini Group Policy processing.

T1555.name: Credentials from Password Stores
T1555.reason: pbeesly's interactive PowerShell (PID 2976) on scranton.dmevals.local opened lsass.exe with 0x1F3FFF and 0x1FFFFF at 03:05:16Z, corroborated by Security 4663, inside a full intrusion chain (registry hijack, shellcode loader, stego IEX, Sysinternals staging, discovery, persistence, cert export, sdelete, WebDAV exfil); wsmprovhost.exe on nashua.dmevals.local also opened lsass with 0x1F3FFF at 03:09:29Z.

T1555.003.name: Credentials from Web Browsers
T1555.003.reason: Only a benign LocalService INetCookies file creation by svchost.exe; no Login Data, logins.json or Local State access by any process, and no browser credential-store references in process creation, 4663 or PowerShell logs.

T1555.004.name: Windows Credential Manager
T1555.004.reason: No cmdkey/vault/credman execution, no registry or file events on Vault/Microsoft\Protect; the only 'Credential' hits were a Credential Guard status message and a PSCredential object used for the WebDAV exfil drive.

T1555.005.name: Password Managers
T1555.005.reason: All password-manager checks (process creation, process access, file creation, 4688, 4104, windows.other) returned zero hits across all four hosts.

T1556.name: Modify Authentication Process
T1556.reason: PowerShell.exe (PID 2976) on scranton opened lsass.exe with 0x1F3FFF/0x1FFFFF and an UNKNOWN call-trace frame at 03:05:16, in the same pbeesly session that ran Get-Keystrokes and Invoke-Exfil; no persistent authentication-process modification was found.

T1556.001.name: Domain Controller Authentication
T1556.001.reason: All lsass accesses on scranton trace to Windows components (wininit, csrss, services, svchost/lsm.dll, Azure telemetry via CorperfmonExt.dll); no 4657/4739/5136 authentication changes.

T1556.002.name: Password Filter DLL
T1556.002.reason: Only Microsoft cryptdll/samlib/samcli DLL loads by normal processes; no Notification Packages registry write, no PasswordFilter DLL, no 4657 on LSA objects.

T1556.005.name: Reversible Encryption
T1556.005.reason: The single Set-ADUser script-block hit is the Microsoft xActiveDirectory DSC module help text on newyork; no 4739 events or reversible-encryption commands.

T1556.006.name: Multi-Factor Authentication
T1556.006.reason: No MFA/authentication-policy modification events (4739 query returned zero hits).

T1556.007.name: Hybrid Identity
T1556.007.reason: No 5136 directory-object modifications; only routine dsregcmd.exe activity on newyork.

T1556.008.name: Network Provider DLL
T1556.008.reason: No 4657 events for NetworkProvider/Winlogon/Credential objects; retrieved Winlogon/Lsa registry writes are routine system values.

T1557.name: Adversary-in-the-Middle
T1557.reason: No interception/relay infrastructure: single NTLM type-3 logon for pbeesly on scranton tied to concurrent PsExec service installs; all 4697 service installs are pbeesly PSEXESVC/javamtsup or per-user svchost services; zeek SMB is normal Kerberos SMB to the DC with only rejected 192.168.0.4 attempts.

T1557.001.name: Name Resolution Poisoning and SMB Relay
T1557.001.reason: Only two unanswered NetBIOS name queries to 10.0.1.255 (S0); all DNS answers come from the legitimate DC 10.0.0.4; no Responder/Inveigh/LLMNR script blocks or EnableMulticast registry changes; SMB sessions are Kerberos/GSSAPI authenticated.

T1557.002.name: ARP Cache Poisoning
T1557.002.reason: No ARP manipulation: ipconfig/route executions on scranton are read-only commands spawned by Azure guest/telemetry agents; no arp/netsh PowerShell; no host mediating traffic between many peers in zeek.

T1557.003.name: DHCP Spoofing
T1557.003.reason: No DHCP server/lease events (1341/1342/1020/1063) and no dhcp-related PowerShell; DNS/DHCP resolution stays with the legitimate DC 10.0.0.4.

T1558.name: Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets
T1558.reason: 326 lsass process-access events are dominated by svchost.exe/AntimalwareConfig.exe/WindowsAzureTelemetryService.exe with 0x1000/0x1400; the 5 full-access grants (powershell.exe on scranton, wsmprovhost.exe on nashua) have managed-code/.NET call traces, not dumping-tool traces. No 4104 script block references kerberos/ticket/krbtgt/mimikatz. Zeek kerberos shows only normal AS/TGS traffic from pbeesly.

T1558.001.name: Golden Ticket
T1558.001.reason: No krbtgt/golden references in PowerShell (0 hits), no KRBTGT hash extraction from lsass, and krbtgt/DMEVALS.LOCAL TGS requests are the normal renewal pair following a successful preauthenticated AS-REP. 4672 privileged logons are only the NEWYORK$ machine account.

T1558.002.name: Silver Ticket
T1558.002.reason: Only 11 TGS requests, all from pbeesly/DMEVALS.LOCAL, to 5 distinct services spread over 16 minutes - ordinary SMB/LDAP/HTTP access. No silver/service-ticket strings in PowerShell and no service-account hash harvesting from lsass.

T1558.003.name: Kerberoasting
T1558.003.reason: No SPN/Kerberoast strings in any 4104 script block (0 hits) and no burst of TGS requests for many SPNs. pbeesly's Kerberos type-3 logons to newyork/nashua from 10.0.1.4 reflect lateral movement from the compromised scranton host, not ticket harvesting.

T1558.004.name: AS-REP Roasting
T1558.004.reason: All 7 AS-REQ events with errors are KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_REQUIRED, each followed within milliseconds by a successful AS-REP - normal preauthentication. No ASREP/GetNPUsers/preauth strings in PowerShell or sysmon command lines (0 hits).

T1606.name: Forge Web Credentials
T1606.reason: No forged web credential activity. 4648 explicit-credential logons are PsExec administration (scranton pbeesly -> NASHUA, PSEXESVC.exe) plus routine winlogon/wininit/taskhostw self-logon events; 4624 logons use only Kerberos/Negotiate/NTLM. The lone 'token' PowerShell hit is SysinternalsSuite readme.ps1 enumerating SE_GROUP_* token attribute constants.

T1606.001.name: Web Cookies
T1606.001.reason: Only cookie artifacts are WebDAV DavSetCookie rundll32 invocations by pbeesly against http://192.168.0.4/webdav and a svchost-created INetCookies cache file under a LocalService package profile. No browser cookie store access or cookie-forging script (C288 zero hits).

T1606.002.name: SAML Tokens
T1606.002.reason: Zero hits for SAML/ADFS/NotOnOrAfter/token-signing in PowerShell script blocks and windows.other messages; no SAML/ADFS file artifacts; authentication packages limited to Kerberos/Negotiate/NTLM. Only identity DNS was login.live.com from svchost (normal Windows behaviour).

T1621.name: Multi-Factor Authentication Request Generation
T1621.reason: No MFA/2FA request generation activity in any dataset. The only related hits were 5 legitimate Microsoft-signed dsregcmd.exe executions by NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM from svchost.exe (Task Scheduler) for Azure AD device registration on nashua, scranton and newyork. No MFA/authenticator/Connect-MsolService/login.microsoftonline strings in PowerShell 4104 script blocks or 4688 command lines, no MFA messages in windows.other, no 4625 failures, and no DNS/network traffic to identity providers (only routine Microsoft telemetry). The concurrent malicious pbeesly activity (PSEXESVC-spawned python.exe beaconing to 192.168.0.4:8443, sdelete64) is credential use/lateral movement, not T1621.

T1649.name: Steal or Forge Authentication Certificates
T1649.reason: On scranton.dmevals.local, user pbeesly ran a PowerShell Get-PrivateKeys function that enumerated cert:\LocalMachine and exported every certificate with Export-PfxCertificate to a password-protected .pfx ("saribas"); Sysmon confirmed creation of C:\Users\pbeesly\Downloads\coyn5igj.3io.pfx by powershell.exe, and an Invoke-BeachCleanup script block plus Sysmon event 23 show the pfx being deleted minutes later. A separate root-store certificate Blob modification on nashua (4657, Sysmon.exe) is suspicious but unconfirmed; no PKINIT/certificate-based logons were observed.

findings.title: Credential-access tooling staged on scranton (fake .scr in C:\ProgramData\victim, sdelete64 anti-forensics) alongside the LSASS access
findings.summary: On scranton.dmevals.local, user pbeesly executed C:\ProgramData\victim\…cod.3aka3.scr (launched by explorer.exe with /S) at 02:55:56, then enumerated the folder with 'gci C:\programdata\victim\' and deleted the file with Sysinternals sdelete64.exe at 03:02:04; further sdelete64 runs wiped Draft.Zip and SysinternalsSuite.zip. On nashua.dmevals.local the same pattern continued with C:\Windows\Temp\sdelete64.exe deleting Rar.exe and working.zip. No 4104 script block in windows.powershell mentions kerberos, ticket, krbtgt, golden, silver, SPN, ASREP or mimikatz (0 hits). The 4104 blocks that do exist on scranton are a reflective shellcode loader (GetProcAddress/GetModuleHandle + base64 PE), which is code execution, not ticket theft. Zeek kerberos (2020-04-30, non-overlapping window) shows only 35 events: 14 AS and 11 TGS requests, all from pbeesly, with 7 KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_REQUIRED that are immediately followed by successful AS-REP - normal preauthentication, not roasting. The only lsass full-access events are the PowerShell/wsmprovhost managed-code accesses described above, whose call traces run through .NET managed assemblies rather than a dumping tool. Zeek kerberos shows krbtgt/DMEVALS.LOCAL service requests only as the normal AS-REP/TGS-renewal pair from pbeesly (e.g. AS at 00:24:19.110 with KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_REQUIRED followed 9ms later by a successful AS-REP, then a TGS to krbtgt/DMEVALS.LOCAL at 00:24:19.124). 4672 privileged logons are all the machine account NEWYORK$ with its standard privilege set, and 4634 logoffs are 227 type-3 / 9 type-2 - no anomalous forged-session pattern.

findings.title: No silver ticket indicators; TGS requests are ordinary service access by pbeesly
findings.summary: Zeek kerberos shows 11 TGS requests, all from client pbeesly/DMEVALS.LOCAL, to cifs/NASHUA (4), host/nashua.dmevals.local (3), cifs/NEWYORK (1), HTTP/NASHUA (1), ldap/NEWYORK.dmevals.local (1) and krbtgt/DMEVALS.LOCAL (1). These are single, spaced-out service-ticket requests (00:24 to 00:40) consistent with normal SMB/LDAP/HTTP access, not a burst of service-ticket acquisition. No 4104 script block mentions silver or 'service ticket' (0 hits), and no lsass access by a service-account-harvesting tool was found. The 4672 privileged logons are only the NEWYORK$ machine account.

findings.title: No Kerberoasting: no SPN enumeration or RC4 TGS burst; pbeesly activity is compromised-host lateral movement
findings.summary: Kerberoasting requires a burst of TGS requests for many SPNs, typically with RC4 encryption. Zeek shows only 11 TGS requests total, all from pbeesly/DMEVALS.LOCAL, spread over 16 minutes and targeting only 5 distinct services - not a roasting pattern. No 4104 script block contains SPN or Kerberoast (0 hits). Note however that pbeesly is the account running attacker tooling on scranton.dmevals.local (cod.3aka3.scr -> cmd -> powershell -> csc.exe) and making Kerberos type-3 network logons to newyork.dmevals.local from 10.0.1.4 (03:04:04, 03:09:04, 03:20:46) and to nashua.dmevals.local - that is lateral movement with a valid ticket, not ticket harvesting.

findings.title: No AS-REP roasting: all AS-REQs are preauthenticated and succeed
findings.summary: AS-REP roasting requires AS-REQ for accounts with preauthentication disabled, returning an encrypted AS-REP without a prior KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_REQUIRED. In zeek, all 7 AS-REQ events carrying an error show KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_REQUIRED (pbeesly/dmevals and pbeesly/DMEVALS.LOCAL), and each is followed within milliseconds by a successful AS-REP - the normal preauthenticated flow. No 4104 script block mentions ASREP, GetNPUsers or preauth (0 hits), and no sysmon process command line contains asrep/GetNPUsers (0 hits).

findings.title: No forged web credential activity; explicit-credential logons are PsExec remote administration
findings.summary: Across windows.security, windows.sysmon, windows.powershell and windows.other (2020-05-02 02:55-03:28Z) there is no evidence of forged web credentials. The 15 event 4648 explicit-credential logons are a repeating administrative pattern: user pbeesly on scranton.dmevals.local (source 10.0.1.6) targeting server NASHUA, matched on nashua.dmevals.local by C:\Windows\PSEXESVC.exe logons for pbeesly to localhost, plus routine DWM-1/UMFD-0/UMFD-1/UMFD-2/SCRANTON$ winlogon/wininit/taskhostw self-logon events. 4624 logons use only Kerberos (217), Negotiate (78) and NTLM (1) with no anomalous authentication package. The single PowerShell 4104 hit matching 'token' is the SysinternalsSuite readme.ps1 script (win.Path C:\Program Files\SysinternalsSuite\readme.ps1) that enumerates SE_GROUP_* access-token attribute constants via Get-AttributesMask - token-attribute documentation, not credential forging. Rare process-access rights (0x1fffff, 0x1f3fff, 0x101541) belong to csrss.exe, services.exe, svchost.exe and wsmprovhost.exe against normal OS targets (svchost, conhost, wmiprvse, RuntimeBroker, taskhostw), i.e. standard OS/management behaviour.

findings.title: Cookie-related artifacts are WebDAV DavSetCookie and a Windows INetCookies cache file, not forged browser cookies
findings.summary: The only cookie-related events are (1) six 4688 process creations on scranton.dmevals.local by user pbeesly running 'rundll32.exe C:\windows\system32\davclnt.dll,DavSetCookie 192.168.0.4 http://192.168.0.4/webdav' between 03:08:50 and 03:10:23Z - the WebDAV client setting an authentication cookie for a WebDAV share, a normal Windows WebDAV access pattern; and (2) one Sysmon event 11 on scranton.dmevals.local at 03:21:05Z where C:\windows\System32\svchost.exe (SYSTEM) created C:\Windows\ServiceProfiles\LocalService\AppData\Local\Packages\warp_jit_db4a1097-b484-4973-bbf2-a04208ecd4d4\AC\INetCookies, a per-package WinINet cookie cache file. No browser cookie store (Cookies/Login Data/Local State) was created or accessed, and no PowerShell script block referenced cookies (C288 zero hits). Nothing indicates cookie theft or forgery.

findings.title: No SAML token forging indicators; no ADFS/SAML artifacts or token-signing references
findings.summary: No SAML/ADFS activity was observed. Searches for SAML/ADFS/NotOnOrAfter/token-signing in PowerShell script blocks (C292) and in windows.other messages (C293) returned zero hits, and no file creations matched saml/adfs names. 4624 logons on all four hosts use only Kerberos, Negotiate and NTLM authentication packages with no rare or forged-token package. The only external identity-related DNS lookups were login.live.com resolved by svchost.exe on scranton and nashua at 03:05:31-32Z, which is normal Windows consumer-account/telemetry behaviour, not SAML token issuance or forgery.

The only T1621-relevant hits were 5 process creations of C:\Windows\System32\dsregcmd.exe on nashua.dmevals.local, scranton.dmevals.local and newyork.dmevals.local between 2020-05-02T03:06:14Z and 03:25:30Z. The full event for the nashua instance (03:25:30.859Z) shows the genuine Microsoft-signed binary (Company 'Microsoft Corporation', Description 'DSREG commandline tool', SHA256 4921B19D3C43CC0CF9921CC37AC0ADF10CEDF20C61AA52F7FC8BA6E717168635) launched as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM from svchost.exe -k netsvcs -p -s Schedule (Task Scheduler) with the standard placeholder command line 'C:\windows\System32\dsregcmd.exe $(Arg0) $(Arg1) $(Arg2)'. This is normal Azure AD/device-registration maintenance, not adversary-driven MFA prompt generation. No MFA/2FA/authenticator content was found in any PowerShell 4104 script block, no MFA-related messages in windows.other, no 4625 failures, and no command line referencing MFA, Connect-MsolService, login.microsoftonline or any identity provider. DNS/network activity to Microsoft endpoints was limited to routine telemetry (v10/v20.events.data.microsoft.com, watson.telemetry.microsoft.com, store-images.s-microsoft.com, checkappexec.microsoft.com, go.microsoft.com) from svchost.exe, WerFault.exe, BackgroundTransferHost.exe, smartscreen.exe and powershell.exe; no okta/duo/login endpoints were contacted. Separately, the same window contains clearly malicious pbeesly activity on nashua.dmevals.local (PSEXESVC-spawned C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe making hundreds of connections to 192.168.0.4:8443, plus sdelete64.exe wiping archives), but that is credential use/lateral movement, not MFA request generation.
findings.title: No MFA request generation observed; dsregcmd hits are routine Azure AD device registration

findings.summary: All 14 Kerberos TGT requests (event 4768) in the window, on newyork.dmevals.local, carry win.PreAuthType = 2 (password pre-authentication) — 9 for pbeesly from 10.0.1.4/10.0.1.6 and 5 for the SCRANTON$ machine account from 10.0.1.4. No PKINIT (PreAuthType 16) or certificate-based authentication was observed, so there is no evidence in this dataset that a stolen or forged certificate was used to obtain tickets. The remaining 4657 registry writes are WMI Autologger/EventLog-Application value changes by wevtutil.exe on scranton, unrelated to certificate stores.
findings.title: Kerberos TGT requests show only password pre-authentication (PreAuthType 2), no PKINIT certificate logons

incidents.title: LSASS memory access with full-access rights by hidden PowerShell on SCRANTON (and via WinRM on NASHUA)
incidents.rationale: All describe the same action: PowerShell.exe PID 2976 (pbeesly, spawned by control.exe stager) opened lsass.exe with 0x1F3FFF/0x1FFFFF and read process memory on scranton, with UNKNOWN call-trace frames; F19 is the same LSASS-access pattern via wsmprovhost.exe on nashua during the pbeesly remote session. Best fit is LSASS Memory (T1003.001).

incidents.title: SAM server full-access handle requests on SCRANTON
incidents.rationale: 4656 events show SAM_SERVER handles with 0xf003f requested by lsass.exe; consistent with Security Account Manager access, though brokered by lsass and not confirmed as dumping. Best fit T1003.002.

incidents.title: Screen-capture loop writing BMPs to Downloads on SCRANTON
incidents.rationale: Invoke-ScreenCapture loop capturing the desktop to BMP files is GUI input capture; best in-scope fit is GUI Input Capture (T1056.002).

incidents.title: Forced-authentication artifacts: Folder handler hijack and StartUp hostui.lnk on SCRANTON
incidents.rationale: Same action: PowerShell planted HKCU Folder\shell\open\command hijack and StartUp hostui.lnk, and later launched hostui.exe. Forced Authentication (T1187) fits the handler-hijack/forced-auth mechanism.

incidents.title: accesschk.exe writing passwordsDB in SysinternalsSuite on SCRANTON
incidents.rationale: File named passwordsDB created by accesschk.exe in the malicious session; content unobserved, so unconfirmed credential store. Best fit Unsecured Credentials (T1552).

incidents.title: Credential-bearing file harvesting, archiving, and plaintext-password lateral use (SCRANTON to NASHUA)
incidents.rationale: Same action chain: enumeration of credential-named files and Compress-Archive/Rar staging on scranton and nashua, plus use of the plaintext domain password Fl0nk3rt0n!T0by with PsExec64. Credentials In Files (T1552.001) fits the observed credential collection from files.

incidents.title: Get-PrivateKeys export of LocalMachine certificate private keys to .pfx on SCRANTON
incidents.rationale: Both describe the same Get-PrivateKeys script block exporting cert:\LocalMachine certificates to password-protected .pfx files in Downloads and subsequent cleanup. Best fit is Steal or Forge Authentication Certificates (T1649).

incidents.title: Root certificate store Blob modification on NASHUA by Sysmon.exe
incidents.rationale: Single 4657 event modifying a ROOT certificate Blob; no corroborating theft. Best fit Steal or Forge Authentication Certificates (T1649).

incidents.title: Credential-access tooling staging and anti-forensic cleanup on SCRANTON and NASHUA
incidents.rationale: Fake .scr staging, folder enumeration, and sdelete64 wiping of tooling/archives is defense evasion/indicator removal, not credential access; best ATT&CK fit is T1070.
